assessment: direct auth expiry, policy/revocation and rate-limit tests; no cryptographic or exploit proof
remaining: No new abstract authentication model replaces protocol/security tests; trusted-single-user and supported deployment assumptions remain unchanged.
evidenceDecision: Real HTTP tests exercise authentication, PIN/rate budgets, cookies and browser admission; real request/response semantics are the security boundary. v0.8.5: Configured passwords accept 8–1024 Unicode characters with a recommendation warning below 15. Direct boundary tests cover ASCII/Unicode and CLI/environment ingestion; session, Origin and throttling evidence remains mandatory. Agent CLI (FM-WORLDCLI): the `/api/world/cli` bearer path is tested directly for loopback-only, no-Origin admission, a derived CLI token that the login credential cannot replace, wrong and missing tokens, and a throttle that never blocks the owner's login. Pane attribution is a pure check of the caller's process ancestry against Herdr's pane process info, tested with spoofed panes, a second connection on the same port from another loopback address, ambiguous rows, shared sockets, IPv6, unknown processes and remote hosts. End to end in a throwaway Herdr session, an in-pane call was verified and the same pane ID from another process was not; the port-collision case is covered only by the synthetic /proc tests. No ordering or recovery protocol is added, so a model would restate these checks. Owner ask withdrawal (#472) compares the verified original connection, runtime, terminal and agent-session digest. Service regressions cover cause-key deduplication, foreign/unverified refusal, idempotent withdrawal, answer preservation and rejection of later answers; the existing endpoint/process ownership fixtures remain mandatory. Per-World cookie (#1250): the session cookie is named per browser-visible port; direct tests cover two Worlds with different secrets sharing one host's cookie jar (unit and real HTTP), a session moving once from the legacy shared name or an earlier port without changing its token, logout clearing every name holding the session, and return paths refusing other origins, `//`, backslashes, control characters, dot-segment normalisation to `//` and `token`. No ordering or recovery state is added: admission is a pure function of the request's cookies.
